The test image shows soybean stems with prominent reddish-brown to dark brown lesions extending along the lower stem portions. Dead/wilted plant material at top, with soil visible at base. Key features: stem discoloration, reddish-brown lesions extending upward on multiple stems.

Top candidates: Phytophthora (dark brown stem lesion from taproot upward), Rhizoctonia (reddish-brown lesions at soil line), Diaporthe (sunken cankers with reddish margins).

Let me check one more reference for comparison:

**Analysis:**

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean stems with prominent reddish-brown discoloration extending from the lower stem sections upward along multiple stems
- One stem still has green tissue; others appear dead/dying
- Lesions extend over a significant length of the lower stem (multiple nodes)
- No black specks (pycnidia), no white mold, no pustules visible
- Soil level at base; plants appear to be wilting/collapsing

**Reference image comparisons:**
- **Phytophthora**: Shows dark brown lesion extending from lower stem upward — matches the extensive stem discoloration pattern in the test image
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows reddish-brown lesions but more localized at the soil line/hypocotyl — color matches well but lesions in test extend higher
- **Diaporthe**: Gray-brown cankers with reddish margins and possible white interior — not a good match (different color pattern)
- **Anthracnose**: Dark blotches on mature/dried plant tissue at late season — not a good match

**Key decision**: The reddish-brown discoloration extending upward from the lower stem across multiple nodes aligns best with **Phytophthora** root and stem rot, which characteristically produces "a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes." The Rhizoctonia pattern is more localized at the soil line, while what we see extends significantly higher on the stems.
